extracted.intended_audience: Hacker News users (people submitting stories and posting comments)
extracted.subtask_description: Rules and community norms for submitting links/posts and participating in comment threads on Hacker News, covering topicality, submission formatting, promotion, and expected tone/behavior in comments.

rubrics_metrics.name: On-Topic
rubrics_metrics.description: On-Topic: Anything that good hackers would find interesting. That includes more than hacking and startups. If you had to reduce it to a sentence, the answer might be: anything that gratifies one's intellectual curiosity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Broad encouragement to submit items that stimulate intellectual curiosity of the HN audience; signals that topic scope goes beyond narrow tech/startup topics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Off-Topic
rubrics_metrics.description: Off-Topic: Most stories about politics, or crime, or sports, or celebrities, unless they're evidence of some interesting new phenomenon.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If they'd cover it on TV news, it's probably off-topic — avoid general-interest news unless it reveals a novel phenomenon relevant to the community.

rubrics_metrics.name: Don't use attention-grabbing formatting in titles
rubrics_metrics.description: Please don't do things to make titles stand out, like using uppercase or exclamation points, or saying how great an article is.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid stylized/advertorial title text; titles should be plain and not promotional.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submit the original source
rubrics_metrics.description: Please submit the original source. If a post reports on something found on another site, submit the latter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prefer linking to primary source material rather than secondary reports.

rubrics_metrics.name: Don't use HN primarily for promotion
rubrics_metrics.description: Please don't use HN primarily for promotion. It's ok to post your own stuff part of the time, but the primary use of the site should be for curiosity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Self-promotion is tolerated sparingly; the community expects posts to be shared for interest rather than marketing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Remove site name from title
rubrics_metrics.description: If the title includes the name of the site, please take it out, because the site name will be displayed after the link.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid redundant site-name text in titles since the UI already shows the source.

rubrics_metrics.name: Crop gratuitous numbers/adjectives in titles
rubrics_metrics.description: If the title contains a gratuitous number or number + adjective, we'd appreciate it if you'd crop it. E.g. translate '10 Ways To Do X' to 'How To Do X,' and '14 Amazing Ys' to 'Ys.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exception: when the number is meaningful, e.g. 'The 5 Platonic Solids.' The goal is to remove clickbait-y listicle framing unless the number is substantive.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use original title unless misleading or linkbait
rubrics_metrics.description: Otherwise please use the original title, unless it is misleading or linkbait; don't editorialize.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Preserve original author/title integrity unless it misrepresents the content; avoid adding editorial spin.

rubrics_metrics.name: Label videos and PDFs in titles
rubrics_metrics.description: If you submit a video or pdf, please warn us by appending [video] or [pdf] to the title.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Helps set expectations for content type and avoid surprise.

rubrics_metrics.name: Don't post announcements or directives
rubrics_metrics.description: Please don't post on HN to ask or tell us something. Send it to hn@ycombinator.com.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid using HN as a bulletin board for requests/notifications directed at the site operators.

rubrics_metrics.name: Don't delete and repost
rubrics_metrics.description: Please don't delete and repost. Deletion is for things that shouldn't have been submitted in the first place.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid reposting same content to game visibility; deletion should be used sparingly and only for erroneous/unsuitable posts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Don't solicit votes/comments/submissions
rubrics_metrics.description: Don't solicit upvotes, comments, or submissions. Users should vote and comment when they run across something they personally find interesting—not for promotion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not request or coordinate voting or engagement; organic interest should drive interactions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Be kind and avoid snark in comments
rubrics_metrics.description: Be kind. Don't be snarky. Converse curiously; don't cross-examine. Edit out swipes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Favor constructive, curious conversation over sarcasm or confrontational tone.

rubrics_metrics.name: Increase thoughtfulness on divisive topics
rubrics_metrics.description: Comments should get more thoughtful and substantive, not less, as a topic gets more divisive.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Encourages deeper, higher-quality contributions when discussions are heated.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reply to arguments, not ad hominems
rubrics_metrics.description: When disagreeing, please reply to the argument instead of calling names. 'That is idiotic; 1 + 1 is 2, not 3' can be shortened to '1 + 1 is 2, not 3.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Focus on addressing claims and reasoning rather than insulting the person.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid being curmudgeonly or generically negative
rubrics_metrics.description: Don't be curmudgeonly. Thoughtful criticism is fine, but please don't be rigidly or generically negative.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Critique should be specific and constructive rather than reflexively dismissive.

rubrics_metrics.name: No generated or AI-edited comments
rubrics_metrics.description: Don't post generated comments or AI-edited comments. HN is for conversation between humans.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explicit prohibition on machine-generated or heavily AI-assisted comment content.

rubrics_metrics.name: Don't fulminate or sneer
rubrics_metrics.description: Please don't fulminate. Please don't sneer, including at the rest of the community.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid dramatic moralizing, denunciations, or dismissive sneering.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assume good faith and charitable interpretation
rubrics_metrics.description: Please respond to the strongest plausible interpretation of what someone says, not a weaker one that's easier to criticize. Assume good faith.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Engage charitably and avoid straw-manning others' points.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid flamebait, tangents, and internet tropes
rubrics_metrics.description: Eschew flamebait. Avoid generic tangents. Omit internet tropes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not derail threads with provocative bait, off-topic rants, or cliché meme responses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid shallow dismissals; teach something
rubrics_metrics.description: Please don't post shallow dismissals, especially of other people's work. A good critical comment teaches us something.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Aim for comments that add information, reasoning, or insight rather than terse dismissal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Don't use HN for political/ideological battles
rubrics_metrics.description: Please don't use Hacker News for political or ideological battle. It tramples curiosity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Discourage partisan campaigning or ideological fighting that undermines the site's purpose.

rubrics_metrics.name: Don't comment about whether someone read an article
rubrics_metrics.description: Please don't comment on whether someone read an article. 'Did you even read the article? It mentions that' can be shortened to 'The article mentions that'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid meta-accusations about reading; instead cite the article or quote relevant passage succinctly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Don't pick the most provocative detail to complain about
rubrics_metrics.description: Please don't pick the most provocative thing in an article or post to complain about in the thread. Find something interesting to respond to instead.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Encourages engaging with substantive or constructive aspects rather than sensational snippets.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limit use of throwaway accounts
rubrics_metrics.description: Throwaway accounts are ok for sensitive information, but please don't create accounts routinely. HN is a community—users should have an identity that others can relate to.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use persistent identities to foster community trust; only use throwaways when necessary for safety/privacy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Don't use uppercase for emphasis; use asterisks
rubrics_metrics.description: Please don't use uppercase for emphasis. Instead, put *asterisks* around it and it will get italicized.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use site formatting conventions rather than all-caps shouting; points to further formatting info.

rubrics_metrics.name: Don't allege astroturfing/shilling publicly
rubrics_metrics.description: Please don't post insinuations about astroturfing, shilling, brigading, foreign agents, and the like. It degrades discussion and is usually mistaken.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you're worried about abuse, email hn@ycombinator.com and they'll look at the data instead of publicly accusing users.

rubrics_metrics.name: Flag spam or off-topic stories; don't feed them
rubrics_metrics.description: If a story is spam or off-topic, flag it. Don't feed egregious comments by replying; flag them instead. If you flag, please don't also comment that you did.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use moderation tools rather than replying to amplify problematic posts; avoid meta-comments about flagging.

rubrics_metrics.name: Don't complain about tangential annoyances
rubrics_metrics.description: Please don't complain about tangential annoyances—e.g. article or website formats, name collisions, or back-button breakage. They're too common to be interesting.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid low-value gripe threads about minor usability or formatting issues of linked sites.

rubrics_metrics.name: Don't comment about voting patterns
rubrics_metrics.description: Please don't comment about the voting on comments. It never does any good, and it makes boring reading.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid meta-discussion focused on votes rather than content.

rubrics_metrics.name: Don't claim HN is turning into Reddit
rubrics_metrics.description: Please don't post comments saying that HN is turning into Reddit. It's a semi-noob illusion, as old as the hills.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Discourage nostalgic complaints about site changes framed as 'turning into Reddit.'
